text:
chris: Heads-up: this morning we saw a short but brutal GPU burst in us-west-2 around 09:12 — queues spiked even though warm-pool hit target. Was admission gating too loose?

katie: Saw it. p95 token latency jumped, and queue head times hit >2s for a few minutes. Autoscaler logs show provisioning lag ~38s; AZ had spot contention.

autoscale-bot: [ALERT] warm_pool_below_target us-west-2-gpu-pool (current=4, target=8) — launched 4 spot instances.

liam: If spots didn't come up fast enough, our admission should've tightened earlier. I suspect the token-bucket refill is tuned to allow big burst credits — we briefly admitted a ton of small requests which inflated batching and slowed everyone.

maria: Replayed traces — most requests were short (<50 tokens) but high concurrency. Because batch_timeout was at 40ms, batches got large while waiting and batching added >200ms per request during the spike.

chris: Proposal: introduce a "burst_gate" mode that proactively reduces burst credits when warm_pool < 50% and increases queue_head_shed to favor fast-fail over long queuing. Also drop batch_timeout to 15ms in that mode.

katie: +1. Canary plan: enable burst_gate only in us-west-2 for 1 AZ, add metric admission_rejects_by_policy and a rollback trigger if 5xx rate increases > 0.5% over baseline.

liam: Config sketch for canary: ```json
{"region":"us-west-2","az":"a","burst_gate":true,"burst_credit_rate":0.5,"batch_timeout_ms":15,"queue_shepherd_threshold_ms":1200}
```

maria: Also recommend a tiered fallback: when warm_pool < 30% mark top-10 customers to use dedicated capacity (if contracted) or shed non-critical traffic. Yes it's more expensive, but avoids SLA breaches. Add cost flag to alerts so SRE can approve fallback.

ops-bot: Created runbook entry: https://docs.internal/redwood/runbooks/scale-burst-gate. Assigned to @katie for canary rollout and monitoring.

chris: Plan timeline: run staging load test today, roll canary 10:00-11:00 PT, observe p50/p95 latency, admission rejects, queued token-ms. If stable for 30m, expand to additional AZs. If 5xx or errors spike, immediate rollback. Also prepare notebook to quantify cost delta for dedicated fallback.

katie: :thumbsup: I'll push the canary config, run the staging test at 09:30 PT, and post results here. If we see improved tail latency without increased error rate we proceed.

maria: One more ask — add a short-lived histogram for provisioning lag per AZ so we can auto-deprioritize AZs with chronic spot delays. That would make the gate smarter.

chris: Good call. We'll add it to the metric set and include in the canary dashboard. Thanks everyone.
